svg.aria-label: The seven assumption checks sorted into two classes: failures that bias coefficients and failures that only break the standard errors
svg.text: A FAILED CHECK IS NOT ONE KIND OF PROBLEM
Sort every failure by what it actually costs you. The two classes have different fixes and different urgency.
a check FAILS
CLASS 1 BIASED COEFFICIENTS
The number you would quote is simply wrong.
Robust standard errors do not help. You must respecify.
functional form (Ramsey RESET)
naive 436.0 -> specified 106.3. fix: log the target, log the area,
add the quadratic age term
omitted variable (found via GBM SHAP)
metro_km biased 28.5% (-0.0617 vs true -0.048). fix: add the
metro x premium interaction, error falls to 1.8%
CLASS 2 INFERENCE ONLY
Coefficients stay unbiased. The uncertainty around them is wrong.
Fix the standard errors, or accept the widened interval.
heteroscedasticity (Breusch-Pagan)
fix: HC3 robust errors. Stays FAILED on purpose, and that is fine.
multicollinearity (VIF, condition number)
VIF 355.6 -> 6.6. fix: drop the r=0.999 twin. Predictions unaffected.
normality, independence, influential points: read, rarely decisive
WHAT THIS BUYS, MEASURED ON HELD-OUT DATA
median APE 8.04% -> 4.10% -> 3.77% naive, specified, plus interaction
R squared 0.774 -> 0.784 -> 0.784 the dial that barely moved
coef error n/a -> 7.9% -> 3.9% the dial that mattered
Error fell 53% while R squared moved 1 point. Watching R squared would have told you nothing was happening.
